text: Raj Begum (27 March 1927 – 26 October 2016) was a Kashmiri playback and folk singer known as the "Nightingale" or "Melody Queen" of Kashmir, whose emotive, high-register voice helped normalize women’s public performance in the Valley and popularized Kashmiri poetic traditions for mass audiences. She received the Padma Shri in 2002 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2013. Born in Srinagar on 27 March 1927, she was raised in a modest household where her father encouraged her musical talent from an early age. She began singing at weddings across communities, absorbing Kashmiri folk idioms and performance practices that later influenced her broadcasting career. Introduced to Radio Kashmir Srinagar in the early 1950s and formally joining in 1954, she became one of the station’s defining live voices during an era with limited archival recording and retired in 1986. Her strong, soaring delivery reshaped expectations for women vocalists in Kashmir, broadening space for female public performance. Her repertoire included folk, light classical, ghazal, devotional, and romantic songs, often drawing on Kashmiri poetic traditions. Due to the live nature of early radio, a complete discography is difficult to establish, though selections survive in radio memories and later compilations. Along with contemporary Naseem Akhtar, she helped dismantle social taboos around women singing publicly in Kashmir, opening doors for later generations of women artists on stage and radio. Commentators have likened her cultural stature to emblematic Kashmiri symbols, underscoring how her voice carried classical Kashmiri poetry into popular consciousness. She married Qadir Ganderbali, a senior Jammu and Kashmir Police official (DIG), who predeceased her; Qadir Ganderbali was married prior to his marriage to Raj Begum, and his first wife reportedly developed severe depression following his second marriage and ultimately died in Ganderbal. She lived in the Chanapora area of Srinagar in later years and was survived by a daughter. She died on 26 October 2016 in Srinagar at the age of 89, reportedly at her daughter’s residence in Chanapora, after a period of illness. Tributes from artists and officials hailed her as a cultural icon who gave voice to Kashmiri heritage across seven decades. Beyond radio and concert work, she is associated with playback for the Kashmiri feature film Mehjoor, aligning her voice with cinematic interpretations of Kashmiri poetry; formal catalogs of her film songs remain limited in public sources. The 2025 film Songs of Paradise will be released, following the journey of a Kashmiri woman who dreams of becoming a singer, inspired by the song of Raj Begum. Radio Kashmir Srinagar.
